newsitem.title: INDIA: Police, protesters clash ahead of beauty pageant.
newsitem.headline: Police, protesters clash ahead of beauty pageant.

text.p: Indian police with tear gas and batons clashed with stone-throwing protesters in the southern city of Bangalore on Saturday, only hours before the start of the controversial Miss World beauty pageant.
In three separate demonstrations led by right-wing Hindu nationalists, police said about 500 people had been detained.
Police said up to seven of their colleagues were injured. It was not immediately known how many protesters were injured.

In one protest, a Reuters reporter saw police with batons and tear gas repel protesters throwing stones and marching on the Chinnaswamy cricket stadium, site of the pageant to be seen by a global television audience of two billion people.
The protests blocked traffic for about two hours in Bangalore, the capital of Karnataka -- Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's home state and India's technology centre.
"It's a police state," Ananth Kumar, a member of parliament for the opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), said as he was bundled into the back of a police van.
Before Saturday afternoon's clashes, police said they had detained about 550 people to head off potential trouble at the pageant, due to start at 9.15 p.m. (1545 GMT).
But they said a squad of would-be suicide protesters was still at large.
"It is a most bizarre situation," Julia Morley, the Miss World organiser, said.
Police detained militant Hindu nationalists, communists and other protesters but were still seeking a group of 15 women who threatened to burn themselves alive to protest against the show.
Shortly before midnight (1830 GMT), one of the 88 young women contestants will win the Miss World title, marking the end of two fraught weeks beset by protests.
Bangalore police commissioner S.C. Burman said the city, patrolled by more than 10,000 police and paramilitary troopers, was quiet and there was little response to a strike call.
On Friday, a court ruled the armed forces could be used if needed to keep the peace.
But Miss World organisers remained alarmed by the threat of self-immolation by members of Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women), led by Kinay Narayana Shashikala.
Shashikala has been in hiding since Thursday, but members of the right-wing Hindu nationalist BJP say they are in contact with her.
"We are looking for her. We will take her into custody when we track her down," Burman said.
One man has already turned himself into a human torch to protest against the pageant in India. That was last week in a town in Tamil Nadu state, 270 miles (430 km) from Bangalore.
The protesters say the beauty contest demeans women and threatens Indian culture.

Police were also on guard for a hitherto unknown group calling itself the Indian Tigers, which has claimed responsibility for attacks on the Indian organisers of Miss World and two small bomb blasts in which no one was injured.

Among those detained earlier on Saturday were members of a "front organisation" for the People's War Group (PWG), a Naxalite Maoist rebel movement which has killed several policemen in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh state, Burman said.
Shashikala has said her followers will mingle with the anticipated crowd of 20,000 spectators in Chinnaswamy cricket stadium and set fire to themselves after first taking poison.
Large numbers of police armed with guns and tear gas swarmed around the stadium and mobile patrols scoured the city.
Pramila Nesargi, a state legislator, said she planned a "Miss Poverty, Miss Illiteracy" pageant outside the stadium.
